newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's iron, steel industry seen on upturn in '97.
newsitem.headline: China's iron, steel industry seen on upturn in '97.

text.p: China will expand exports of iron and steel, and consolidate its position as the world's biggest producer of steel, said He Ling, the vice president of China Iron and Steel Industry and Trade Group Corporation (CSGC), on Monday.
"We believe the total value of imports and exports in China will continue to increase this year," He said.
"Looking ahead we are filled with more confidence in 1997. This is because China is now politically stable and its national economy is keeping up a steady increase," He said.
He was speaking at the 10th China Metallurgical Products Export Trade Fair being held in Hong Kong this week, sponsored by CSCG and China Metallurgic (Hong Kong) Ltd Corporation.
Last year China produced over 100 million tonnes of steel which put it in first position in the world, He said.
China exported 4.22 million tonnes and imported 15.99 million tonnes of steel products, He said.
CSGC has more than 110 members and is the largest industry and trade group in iron and steel in China.

The total value of CSCG's exports was US$980 million in 1996 and the value of its imports last year was US$720 million, Jiang Hong, director, senior engineer of CSGC's planning and external trade department.
He was speaking to reporters after the opening ceremony.
"We expected this year's export value to increase slightly but not very much," Jiang said. "Demand from European and South East Asian countries has softened."
